newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debts mixed in moderate trading.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debts mixed in moderate trading.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices turned in a fixed performance, unable to derive direction from rangebound U.S. Treasuries, traders said.
"The Treasuries are dictating our market," a trader said. ""The market is going to drift until the release of the ECI next week."
The U.S. employment cost index for the fourth quarter is scheduled for release next Tuesday at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.
The success of Argentina's $2 billion 20-year global bond priced on Wednesday still riveted attention in the market.
The spread of the new issue tightened by about 25 basis points from the launched price at 462.5 basis points over comparable Treasuries, traders said.
"For many new issues, the spreads tend to tighten a bit when they are freed to trade," said a trader, "but this Argie global seems to do exceptionally well."

The spread is likely to tighten to 400 basis points, if the yield of the 30-year Treasury bond does not spike up to 7.00 percent, he said. The benchmark long bond yield stood at 6.85 percent on Thursday.
Kip Allardt, emerging market debt strategist at CS First Boston, said the success fo the new Argentine global paved the way for future issuance.

"Argentina has huge funding needs and desperately needed a a winner," he said, estimating that the country needs to raise $11 billion this year to meet the current account deficit and debt servicing cost.
But some traders doubted if there is much near-term upside potential left for Argentine Bradies.
Russia papers got a mild boost as traders focused on the planned launch of the country's first mark-denominated eurobond and the closing of the Vnesh restructuring deal.
"The dollar Vnesh has to stay above 80 pull more people from the sidelines," said a trader.
"Spreads on Argie Bradies have tightened by 100 basis points since Christmas," he said. "Now with all the good news out, there's not much driving the market."
Argentina FRBs eased 1/4 to 89-1/2 bid, while Argentina Pars was unchanged to bid at 64-3/4.
Ecuador Bradies were mixed, reflecting divided views on the country's economic reform, traders said.

A trader who is bullish on Ecuador noted while the convertibility plan may be a wild card, firm oil prices and record banana export are boosting Ecuador's position to repay debt. (( -- Nailene Chou Wiest - 212-859-1674))
